title: Forearm rotation: takeaway timing and trail-arm structure

context.body_context: No physical screen or measured mobility

evidence.attribution: Alex Clapp coaching an unnamed student; speaker roles follow visible instruction and responses
evidence.session: Forearm rotation timing and trail-arm structure
evidence.summary: Coach uses an upright demonstration to compare structures. Student first turns with club upright and then adds forward bend; coach says this resembles his usual position without added forearm rotation. They reset, rotate club to roughly parallel with floor while upright, turn, then bend into golf posture. Coach calls this a better club position and contrasts it with right elbow pulling behind and forearm orientation keeping club closed.

Forward bend added to complete second comparison.
Coach points to right elbow relationship.
Contrasting forearm/club position.
Final embedded caption says closed.

limitations: Body-relative hand and shaft geometry shown through guided rehearsal; no calibrated elbow, wrist or face angle. Body occlusion limits some views. Final ASR tail repetitions are excluded from coaching interpretation.

cases.title: Use upper-arm contact to feel later forearm rotation after the takeaway
cases.coaching_finding: Coach identifies early forearm rotation pulling takeaway inside, while also explaining that insufficient rotation later leaves the student in an unwanted top structure with right elbow behind and club closed. These are phase-specific observations from coach testimony.
cases.coach_reasoning: Get the initial takeaway first, then blend forearm rotation with torso turn. Removing rotation throughout the swing loses the later arm/club organization the coach wants.

intervention.drill: Hold club in right hand; place a couple of left fingers behind right arm just above elbow. Reach takeaway, retain light feedback contact and rehearse the demonstrated forearm movement with turn.
intervention.cue: Takeaway first, then blend rotation with turn.
intervention.source_feel: Keep contact/pressure and feel stretching in the demonstrated direction.
intervention.limits: Do not translate tactile pressure into a force target or forcibly clamp the elbow.

applicability: Coach-established correspondence to this timing/arm-structure pattern.
Check initial takeaway separately from later rotation; do not apply a generic more-roll cue from address.
unknowns: Original diagnosis footage, ball-flight complaint, measured angles and physical constraints.
Whether guided rehearsal transfers to normal speed or improves strike/dispersion.
Exact pressure, amount of rotation and definition of a correct takeaway for another golfer.
cases.observed_result: Student performs guided rehearsals and coach approves selected positions. No ball is struck in the extracted lesson.

cases.title: Use upright rotate–turn–bend comparison to explain top structure
cases.coaching_finding: Coach identifies early forearm rotation pulling takeaway inside, while also explaining that insufficient rotation later leaves the student in an unwanted top structure with right elbow behind and club closed. These are phase-specific observations from coach testimony.

intervention.drill: Compare turning with upright club then bending into posture against rotating club roughly horizontal while upright, adding torso turn, then bending.
intervention.cue: Set the arm/club orientation before completing the comparison.
intervention.teaching_purpose: Isolate the contribution of forearm rotation to the final club/arm relationship.
intervention.limits: This is a staged explanatory sequence; it is not the required chronological sequence of a normal backswing.

ASR repeats thats where youre going and thank you many times in fractions of a second. This is treated as transcription artefact, not source speech evidence. Raw output retained; final closed caption is visually supported.
The post description makes broader claims about shallowing, width/depth and wrist conditions. Video supports coach reasoning and guided positions, not measured proof of all advertised benefits.

cross_source_links.relation: Similar teaching decomposition with distinct setup and diagnosis
cross_source_links.explanation: Faldo uses a low wrist preset then turn; Clapp uses an upright arm/club rotation–turn–bend comparison for an identified student pattern. Both split a movement for teaching, but the geometry and eligibility cannot be assumed identical.

cross_source_links.relation: Related inside takeaway finding with different mechanism and intervention
cross_source_links.explanation: Mayson’s student lesson prioritizes width and a shorter backswing. Clapp emphasizes timing of forearm rotation. An inside takeaway label alone does not choose between these cases.

cross_source_links.relation: Rehearsal constraints require normal-swing transfer check
cross_source_links.explanation: Ruffels distinguishes constrained aid appearance from normal motion. Clapp’s upright construction likewise should remain an explanatory rehearsal rather than a normal-swing template.

within_source_distinctions.relationship: Two teaching variants for one timing/structure focus. First uses tactile feedback in posture; second decomposes geometry while upright. Early excessive rotation and missing later rotation must remain phase-specific.

annotation_opportunities: Pair early-takeaway and later-backswing sequences when attaching the word rotation.
Label coach simulation, manually guided student rehearsal and independent student attempt separately.
Mark the feedback hand and approximate upper-arm contact area, without estimating pressure.
Present the two upright comparison sequences side by side with posture stage labels.
excluded_material: Automatic more-forearm-roll recommendation from an inside takeaway alone.
Treating instructor simulated fault as his natural swing.
Measured shallowing, clubface correction or ball-flight improvement.
Treating shift/post demonstration as a separate lower-body diagnosis.

independent_validation.reason: Coach reasoning and guided position feedback are preserved; original swing and ball-flight outcomes absent.
